body:
Every `safe-tier-1` docs PR this cycle has needed a manual `gh pr merge --admin`
despite green CI and a `success` run of `auto-merge.yml`. Observed twice on
2026-08-07: #1450 (opened by the 20:00Z tick, still open and green at 22:22Z)
and #1452 (opened and stalled in the same tick that filed this).

## Mechanism — all four links OBSERVED

1. `auto-merge.yml` evaluates the tier and calls `gh pr merge --auto --squash`,
   which enables GitHub's *native* auto-merge. The run reports `success` — it
   enabled the setting, which is all it claims to do.
2. The `main protection` ruleset (id `15871246`) sets
   `strict_required_status_checks_policy = true`, i.e. a branch must be
   up to date with `main` to merge.
3. `main` receives commits on its own — the `Update Translations` bot is the
   routine one — so an open PR goes `BEHIND` shortly after it is opened.
4. Native auto-merge does **not** update the head branch. Nothing else does
   either. So the PR sits green + `BEHIND` indefinitely.

`gh pr view` reports `mergeable=MERGEABLE` throughout, which is what makes this
easy to miss: the blocking condition shows up only in `mergeStateStatus=BEHIND`.

## Why it matters

The CHANGES-SHA backfill is the last step of every release cycle, and it is
always tier-1, so it always lands in this hole. Each one then needs a human or
a tick to notice and admin-merge it. A tick that does not look will leave the
ledger un-backfilled, which is the record the *next* release reads.

## Options

- Have `auto-merge.yml` call `gh pr update-branch` before enabling auto-merge,
  and re-run on `push` to `main` so it re-updates. Closest to the intent.
- Enable the repo's "Automatically update branch" / auto-update setting so
  GitHub keeps auto-merge candidates current.
- Drop `strict_required_status_checks_policy` for docs-only paths — narrowest
  in effect but weakens the gate for everything sharing the ruleset.

Noticed while shipping #1451 and #1452.

---

## 2026-08-29 — the chosen option was measured, and it does not do what this finding assumed

The operator picked **option 2** ("enable the repo's Automatically update branch setting"):
`allow_update_branch: true`, verified live on the repo object alongside
`strict_required_status_checks_policy: [true]`.

**It does not close this finding.** Two sessions measured it independently on their own PRs:

- CWNG NEW UI DEFAULT (#2021): armed + BEHIND, did not self-update; state only moved after
  `gh api -X PUT .../update-branch` was triggered by hand.
- KINDLE KIDS: five PRs sitting at BEHIND with auto-merge ARMED, none moving on their own.

So GitHub *can* update the branch, but does not do so promptly or automatically for an armed
PR. Link 4 of the mechanism above — "native auto-merge does not update the head branch;
nothing else does either" — **still holds with the setting on.** Arm-and-walk-away still waits
indefinitely, and it presents exactly as a CI timeout, which is very likely what several of
this batch's `ci-timeout` observations actually were.

## The objection to option 1 was raised and retracted — it is clear on BOTH paths

A claim circulated that `gh pr update-branch` cancels auto-merge, which would have ruled option 1
out. It was retracted by its author after measurement, on both code paths:

| path | PR | before | after (t+12/24/36s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gh api -X PUT .../update-branch` (REST) | #2021 | BEHIND, ARMED | BLOCKED, **ARMED** |
| `gh pr update-branch --rebase` (subcommand) | #2014 | BEHIND, ARMED | BLOCKED, **ARMED** |

Head advanced, BEHIND cleared, auto-merge survived in both. **Option 1 is therefore the live
candidate** and needs no re-arm step.

⚠️ Provenance worth keeping, because the error is more reusable than the fact: the original claim
came from seeing five armed PRs at `auto=off` after an uncontrolled sequence — arm, hold,
disable-auto, re-arm, update-branch, and the `allow_update_branch` repo flip all inside one
window — and naming the step that had just run. A correlation across a messy sequence, broadcast
as a mechanism without the 40-second before/after test that later refuted it. **What actually
disarmed those five is still unknown**; the untested candidate is the repo-setting flip itself.
Do not treat a future disarm as explained.

## Scope note: this finding does NOT govern `scripts/lib/pr-lifecycle.sh`

Grepped, not assumed: pr-lifecycle contains no `update-branch` call by either path, and never
arms `--auto`. Line 306 is a bare `gh pr merge --squash --admin --delete-branch`, gated only by
`mergeable == MERGEABLE` at 300-305.

**`--admin` bypasses branch protection, so the server will not catch a stale-base merge — the
caller must.** `BEHIND` *is* `MERGEABLE`, so that precondition sails straight through a base that
has moved. That is the hazard, not a reassurance: `strict_required_status_checks_policy` exists
so we do not merge code verified against a dead base, and with a bypass actor the only thing
enforcing it is the caller's own discipline. Load-bearing at least once this cycle — #2018 landed
changes to `frontend/e2e/fixtures.ts` and `frontend/e2e/README.md`, both also modified by #1956,
whose green was against a base that no longer existed at that moment.

Corollary for anyone using pr-lifecycle with `--merge`: check `mergeStateStatus` yourself before
authorising. `.mergeable` will not tell you.
title: tier-1 auto-merge stalls forever once a PR goes BEHIND
